_comment: Scoping is delegated to the model, so it cannot be asserted mechanically.
What is asserted here is the thing we control: that the transcript handed
to the model marks where the name was spoken, keeps the words on BOTH
sides, and never slices the question up itself. Reviewed by hand; re-run

cases.note: The classic phrasing. Everything after the marker.

cases.utterance: Something has happened, Computer, what is the answer?
cases.marked: Something has happened, «ASSISTANT-NAME-SPOKEN», what is the answer?
cases.note: Both sides survive; the model decides which half is the question.

cases.utterance: Something has happened, what is the answer, Computer?
cases.marked: Something has happened, what is the answer, «ASSISTANT-NAME-SPOKEN»?
cases.note: The phrasing the old split_command() turned into an empty query.

cases.utterance: how long does the warp core take to cool, computer
cases.marked: how long does the warp core take to cool, «ASSISTANT-NAME-SPOKEN»
must_keep: how long does the warp core take to cool
cases.note: No question mark; the classifier must not depend on punctuation.
A bare call for attention: wait for the question rather than dispatching.

cases.utterance: so, computer, remind me what he said about the deflector
cases.marked: so, «ASSISTANT-NAME-SPOKEN», remind me what he said about the deflector
must_keep: remind me what he said about the deflector
cases.note: "so" is filler, so this is still being addressed.

cases.utterance: tell me the time, computer, please
cases.note: Trailing politeness is not a command.

must_not_wake: my computer is broken and he laughed about it
I told him my computer is broken
